decision_basis: CCL11/CCR2b binding, calcium and chemotaxis with antagonist and MCP-1 competition support qualified-high relay/function evidence while retaining partial agonism and high-concentration limits.
CCL17/CCR8 binding, Gi-linked receptor signaling, and immune-cell functional phenotypes support qualified-high relay/function evidence as a noncanonical context-dependent axis.
CD48/CD2 counter-receptor identity, TCR/Lck-proximal activation, and mouse-dominant T-cell function support qualified-high immune adhesion/costimulation relay evidence.
E-cadherin/alphaEbeta7-CD103 adhesion and CTL synapse function support qualified-high integrin-complex relay/function evidence with TCR integration.
